A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LEVIS. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original DC-OPF and MNIST verification experiments, radius distributions, and an appendix study of PCA accuracy and computation time.

after.justification: v2 reports original verification experiments, including MNIST and CIFAR-10 solver timings, optimality gaps, and analyses of search directions and initialization.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a regularized complementarity NLP followed by a reduced MIP. Directional search becomes angle-parameterized, and LEVIS-β gains queued centers, near-surface shifts, input bounds and resampling. As written, Algorithm 1 also changes its first paired boundary search from v1's opposite collinear direction to 90 degrees.

E1.justification: v2 retains IEEE 9-bus DC-OPF and MNIST and adds actual CIFAR-10 evaluation in Table 1. This extends image coverage from handwritten digits to natural RGB objects; the changed MNIST preprocessing is separately a protocol change.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds a MIP baseline strengthened with CROWN bounds for runtime comparison. The Lipschitz-based Lower Bound and Exact Fixed Center comparators remain. CROWN-related citations in v1 did not constitute this evaluated solver comparison.

E3.justification: v1 explicitly uses 50-component PCA inputs for MNIST; v2 describes a 784-input network and makes PCA optional. New experiments introduce runtime and optimality-gap evaluation using a reported 894-neuron configuration, plus controlled sweeps of search angles and initialization shifts. The DC-OPF data generation and 80/20 split are retained.

E4.justification: Sections 5.6–5.7 add sensitivity analyses of search direction, initialization and randomness, plus t-SNE analyses of discovered centers. Conversely, v1's PCA speed–accuracy study and empirical four-iteration union-expansion visualization disappear. The LEVIS-α convergence display retains only the infinity-norm panel, dropping the other two norm-specific traces.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that the radius comparison uses five independently trained models and documents ten seeds or runs for search settings. These disclosures do not establish increased repetitions of earlier experiments. Section 5.3 promises ranges, but Table 2 contains single values. The five-run LEVIS-α mean/standard-deviation practice and appendix radius statistics remain.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds proposed-versus-baseline timings of 1.34 versus 10.48 seconds on MNIST and 5.96 versus 17.47 seconds on CIFAR-10, with gaps 0.004 and 0.0009. Lipschitz radii change from 6.386/6.79/18.22 to 4.52/4.80/12.88, while exact radii remain 16.24/47.28/28.12. Radius-distribution plots are replaced and PCA results removed; these are not established same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: v2 adds the complementarity reformulation and relaxation, active/inactive/bi-active neuron sets, an activation-consistency condition for global optimality, and computational-complexity arguments. These substantially extend the mathematical treatment. The existing LEVIS-α convergence theorem and appendix proof remain essentially unchanged, including the appendix's convexity qualification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion elevate hybrid-solver scalability to a central contribution, claiming up to 6× speedup with a small optimality gap. The abstract also changes LEVIS-α's 'largest possible' ball to a 'single, large' ball and restricts its theoretical-analysis claim to LEVIS-α, whereas v1 named both variants.

C2.justification: v2 introduces conditional applicability of the hybrid solver's optimality guarantee and discusses spurious NLP solutions. It adds interpretations of search-parameter diversity and t-SNE clusters, attributes smaller MNIST radii to dimensionality and network complexity, and gives a cube-coverage rationale for the infinity norm. The non-convex oscillation caveat was already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents Gurobi/Ipopt roles, complementarity regularization, the center-shift factor, MNIST layer widths and initial-image selection, and three machines' specifications. It replaces v1's generic planned release location with a named LEVIS-LANL/LEVIS repository statement. Some earlier information disappears, including the explicit ONNX workflow and detailed PCA reduction study.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around exact preimages and probabilistic safe regions, including Matoba and Fleuret, Marzari and colleagues, and Bell and colleagues. It introduces a complementary optimization literature supporting the new solver, including Yang, Kilwein, Kazi and Scholtes. Several earlier Lipschitz, software and application references are removed; Tjeng's publication update represents the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The method receives a new numbered hierarchy, dataset descriptions move into structured appendices, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added. Authorship and venue formatting also change. This exceeds wording edits associated solely with new scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime and hardware tables and sensitivity/t-SNE figures, revises radius-distribution displays and the center-selection illustration, and reduces the three-panel convergence figure to a small single panel. The grid diagram and adversarial-image example move to the appendix. PCA and empirical union-expansion displays disappear, and appendices change to a single-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful solver comparisons, CIFAR-10 coverage, sensitivity analyses and implementation details. However, its conditional hybrid-solver guarantee in Section 4.2 is not reconciled with unconditional exact-verification claims in Section 5.7. Algorithm 1 also specifies an orthogonal first pair despite the retained collinear-pair convergence rationale. These issues affect the central correctness claim, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment despite the expanded evidence.
